items.chapter: Scene: Thebes. Before the Palace of Oedipus.
items.text: Suppliants of all ages are seated round the altar at the palace doors, at their head a PRIEST OF ZEUS. To them enter OEDIPUS.

items.chapter: Scene: Thebes. Before the Palace of Oedipus.
items.text: for thy zeal of yore Our country’s savior thou art justly hailed: O never may we thus record thy reign:— “He raised us up only to cast us down.” Uplift us, build our city on a rock. Thy happy star ascendant brought us luck, O let it not decline! If thou wouldst rule This land, as now thou reignest, better sure To rule a peopled than a desert realm. Nor battlements nor galleys aught avail, If men to man and guards to guard them tail.

items.chapter: Scene: Thebes. Before the Palace of Oedipus.
items.text: OEDIPUS. We soon shall know; he’s now in earshot range. [Enter CREON] My royal cousin, say, Menoeceus’ child, What message hast thou brought us from the god?

items.chapter: Scene: Thebes. Before the Palace of Oedipus.
items.text: CREON. Let me report then all the god declared. King Phoebus bids us straitly extirpate A fell pollution that infests the land, And no more harbor an inveterate sore.

items.chapter: Scene: Thebes. Before the Palace of Oedipus.
items.text: OEDIPUS. I heard as much, but never saw the man.

items.chapter: Scene: Thebes. Before the Palace of Oedipus.
items.text: OEDIPUS. Was he within his palace, or afield, Or traveling, when Laius met his fate?

items.chapter: Scene: Thebes. Before the Palace of Oedipus.
items.text: CREON. Robbers, he told us, not one bandit but A troop of knaves, attacked and murdered him.

items.chapter: Scene: Thebes. Before the Palace of Oedipus.
items.text: OEDIPUS. Well, _I_ will start afresh and once again Make dark things clear. Right worthy the concern Of Phoebus, worthy thine too, for the dead; I also, as is meet, will lend my aid To avenge this wrong to Thebes and to the god. Not for some far-off kinsman, but myself, Shall I expel this poison in the blood; For whoso slew that king might have a mind To strike me too with his assassin hand. Therefore in righting him I serve myself. Up, children, haste ye, quit these altar stairs, Take hence your suppliant wands, go summon hither The Theban commons. With the god’s good help Success is sure; ’tis ruin if we fail. [Exeunt OEDIPUS and CREON]

items.chapter: Scene: Thebes. Before the Palace of Oedipus.
items.text: (Ant. 2) Wasted thus by death on death All our city perisheth. Corpses spread infection round; None to tend or mourn is found. Wailing on the altar stair Wives and grandams rend the air— Long-drawn moans and piercing cries Blent with prayers and litanies. Golden child of Zeus, O hear Let thine angel face appear!

items.chapter: Scene: Thebes. Before the Palace of Oedipus.
items.text: For, let alone the god’s express command, It were a scandal ye should leave unpurged The murder of a great man and your king, Nor track it home. And now that I am lord, Successor to his throne, his bed, his wife, (And had he not been frustrate in the hope Of issue, common children of one womb Had forced a closer bond twixt him and me, But Fate swooped down upon him), therefore I His blood-avenger will maintain his cause As though he were my sire, and leave no stone Unturned to track the assassin or avenge The son of Labdacus, of Polydore, Of Cadmus, and Agenor first of the race.

items.chapter: Scene: Thebes. Before the Palace of Oedipus.
items.text: CHORUS. May I then say what seems next best to me?

items.chapter: Scene: Thebes. Before the Palace of Oedipus.
items.text: OEDIPUS. So I heard, But none has seen the man who saw him fall.

items.chapter: Scene: Thebes. Before the Palace of Oedipus.
items.text: TEIRESIAS. Alas, alas, what misery to be wise When wisdom profits nothing! This old lore I had forgotten; else I were not here.

items.chapter: Scene: Thebes. Before the Palace of Oedipus.
items.text: OEDIPUS. Oh speak, Withhold not, I adjure thee, if thou know’st, Thy knowledge. We are all thy suppliants.

items.chapter: Scene: Thebes. Before the Palace of Oedipus.
items.text: OEDIPUS. Monster! thy silence would incense a flint. Will nothing loose thy tongue? Can nothing melt thee, Or shake thy dogged taciturnity?

items.chapter: Scene: Thebes. Before the Palace of Oedipus.
items.text: TEIRESIAS. I have no more to say; storm as thou willst, And give the rein to all thy pent-up rage.

items.chapter: Scene: Thebes. Before the Palace of Oedipus.
items.text: OEDIPUS. Who was thy teacher? not methinks thy art.

items.chapter: Scene: Thebes. Before the Palace of Oedipus.
items.text: TEIRESIAS. I say thou art the murderer of the man Whose murderer thou pursuest.

items.chapter: Scene: Thebes. Before the Palace of Oedipus.
items.text: OEDIPUS. Think’st thou for aye unscathed to wag thy tongue?

items.chapter: Scene: Thebes. Before the Palace of Oedipus.
items.text: OEDIPUS. Offspring of endless Night, thou hast no power O’er me or any man who sees the sun.

items.chapter: Scene: Thebes. Before the Palace of Oedipus.
items.text: This is the man whom thou wouldst undermine, In hope to reign with Creon in my stead. Methinks that thou and thine abettor soon Will rue your plot to drive the scapegoat out. Thank thy grey hairs that thou hast still to learn What chastisement such arrogance deserves.

items.chapter: Scene: Thebes. Before the Palace of Oedipus.
items.text: TEIRESIAS. I ne’er had come hadst thou not bidden me.

items.chapter: Scene: Thebes. Before the Palace of Oedipus.
items.text: OEDIPUS. Thou lov’st to speak in riddles and dark words.

items.chapter: Scene: Thebes. Before the Palace of Oedipus.
items.text: OEDIPUS. No matter if I saved the commonwealth.

items.chapter: Scene: Thebes. Before the Palace of Oedipus.
items.text: (Ant. 1) Yea, but now flashed forth the summons from Parnassus’ snowy peak, “Near and far the undiscovered doer of this murder seek!” Now like a sullen bull he roves Through forest brakes and upland groves, And vainly seeks to fly The doom that ever nigh Flits o’er his head, Still by the avenging Phoebus sped, The voice divine, From Earth’s mid shrine. (Str. 2) Sore perplexed am I by the words of the master seer. Are they true, are they false? I know not and bridle my tongue for fear, Fluttered with vague surmise; nor present nor future is clear. Quarrel of ancient date or in days still near know I none Twixt the Labdacidan house and our ruler, Polybus’ son. Proof is there none: how then can I challenge our King’s good name, How in a blood-feud join for an untracked deed of shame?

items.chapter: Scene: Thebes. Before the Palace of Oedipus.
items.text: CHORUS. Such things were said; with what intent I know not.

items.chapter: Scene: Thebes. Before the Palace of Oedipus.
items.text: OEDIPUS. Thou art glib of tongue, but I am slow to learn Of thee; I know too well thy venomous hate.

items.chapter: Scene: Thebes. Before the Palace of Oedipus.
items.text: CREON. Therein thou judgest rightly, but this wrong That thou allegest—tell me what it is.

items.chapter: Scene: Thebes. Before the Palace of Oedipus.
items.text: OEDIPUS. Did the same prophet then pursue his craft?

items.chapter: Scene: Thebes. Before the Palace of Oedipus.
items.text: CREON. Surely full quest was made, but nothing learnt.

items.chapter: Scene: Thebes. Before the Palace of Oedipus.
items.text: OEDIPUS. But for thy prompting never had the seer Ascribed to me the death of Laius.

items.chapter: Scene: Thebes. Before the Palace of Oedipus.
items.text: OEDIPUS. I grant her freely all her heart desires.

items.chapter: Scene: Thebes. Before the Palace of Oedipus.
items.text: No such ambition ever tempted me, Nor would I have a share in such intrigue. And if thou doubt me, first to Delphi go, There ascertain if my report was true Of the god’s answer; next investigate If with the seer I plotted or conspired, And if it prove so, sentence me to death, Not by thy voice alone, but mine and thine. But O condemn me not, without appeal, On bare suspicion. ’Tis not right to adjudge Bad men at random good, or good men bad. I would as lief a man should cast away The thing he counts most precious, his own life, As spurn a true friend. Thou wilt learn in time The truth, for time alone reveals the just; A villain is detected in a day.

items.chapter: Scene: Thebes. Before the Palace of Oedipus.
items.text: CREON. I see thou wilt not yield, nor credit me.

items.chapter: Scene: Thebes. Before the Palace of Oedipus.
items.text: OEDIPUS. Yes, lady; I have caught him practicing Against my royal person his vile arts.

items.chapter: Scene: Thebes. Before the Palace of Oedipus.
items.text: OEDIPUS. Declare it then and make thy meaning plain.

items.chapter: Scene: Thebes. Before the Palace of Oedipus.
items.text: CREON. Thou art as sullen in thy yielding mood As in thine anger thou wast truculent. Such tempers justly plague themselves the most.

items.chapter: Scene: Thebes. Before the Palace of Oedipus.
items.text: CHORUS. Rumors bred unjust suspicious and injustice rankles sore.

items.chapter: Scene: Thebes. Before the Palace of Oedipus.
items.text: OEDIPUS. I will, for thou art more to me than these. Lady, the cause is Creon and his plots.

items.chapter: Scene: Thebes. Before the Palace of Oedipus.
items.text: JOCASTA. Then thou mayest ease thy conscience on that score. Listen and I’ll convince thee that no man Hath scot or lot in the prophetic art. Here is the proof in brief. An oracle Once came to Laius (I will not say ’Twas from the Delphic god himself, but from His ministers) declaring he was doomed To perish by the hand of his own son, A child that should be born to him by me. Now Laius—so at least report affirmed— Was murdered on a day by highwaymen, No natives, at a spot where three roads meet. As for the child, it was but three days old, When Laius, its ankles pierced and pinned Together, gave it to be cast away By others on the trackless mountain side. So then Apollo brought it not to pass The child should be his father’s murderer, Or the dread terror find accomplishment, And Laius be slain by his own son. Such was the prophet’s horoscope. O king, Regard it not.

items.chapter: Scene: Thebes. Before the Palace of Oedipus.
items.text: JOCASTA. So ran the story that is current still.

items.chapter: Scene: Thebes. Before the Palace of Oedipus.
items.text: JOCASTA. ’Twas but a brief while were thou wast proclaimed Our country’s ruler that the news was brought.

items.chapter: Scene: Thebes. Before the Palace of Oedipus.
items.text: OEDIPUS. O woe is me! Mehtinks unwittingly I laid but now a dread curse on myself.

items.chapter: Scene: Thebes. Before the Palace of Oedipus.
items.text: JOCASTA. They were but five in all, and one of them A herald; Laius in a mule-car rode.

items.chapter: Scene: Thebes. Before the Palace of Oedipus.
items.text: OEDIPUS. Fetch him at once. I fain would see the man.

items.chapter: Scene: Thebes. Before the Palace of Oedipus.
items.text: But other grievous things he prophesied, Woes, lamentations, mourning, portents dire; To wit I should defile my mother’s bed And raise up seed too loathsome to behold, And slay the father from whose loins I sprang. Then, lady,—thou shalt hear the very truth— As I drew near the triple-branching roads, A herald met me and a man who sat In a car drawn by colts—as in thy tale— The man in front and the old man himself Threatened to thrust me rudely from the path, Then jostled by the charioteer in wrath I struck him, and the old man, seeing this, Watched till I passed and from his car brought down Full on my head the double-pointed goad. Yet was I quits with him and more; one stroke Of my good staff sufficed to fling him clean Out of the chariot seat and laid him prone. And so I slew them every one.

items.chapter: Scene: Thebes. Before the Palace of Oedipus.
items.text: JOCASTA. Suppose him here, what wouldst thou learn of him?

items.chapter: Scene: Thebes. Before the Palace of Oedipus.
items.text: OEDIPUS. Thou reasonest well. Still I would have thee send And fetch the bondsman hither. See to it.

items.chapter: Scene: Thebes. Before the Palace of Oedipus.
items.text: (Ant. 2) No more I’ll seek earth’s central oracle, Or Abae’s hallowed cell, Nor to Olympia bring My votive offering. If before all God’s truth be not bade plain. O Zeus, reveal thy might, King, if thou’rt named aright Omnipotent, all-seeing, as of old; For Laius is forgot; His weird, men heed it not; Apollo is forsook and faith grows cold. [Enter JOCASTA.]

items.chapter: Scene: Thebes. Before the Palace of Oedipus.
items.text: JOCASTA. My greetings to thee, stranger; thy fair words Deserve a like response. But tell me why Thou comest—what thy need or what thy news.

items.chapter: Scene: Thebes. Before the Palace of Oedipus.
items.text: JOCASTA. What! is not aged Polybus still king?

items.chapter: Scene: Thebes. Before the Palace of Oedipus.
items.text: OEDIPUS. My wife, my queen, Jocasta, why hast thou Summoned me from my palace?

items.chapter: Scene: Thebes. Before the Palace of Oedipus.
items.text: MESSENGER. If I must first make plain beyond a doubt My message, know that Polybus is dead.

items.chapter: Scene: Thebes. Before the Palace of Oedipus.
items.text: OEDIPUS. Out on it, lady! why should one regard The Pythian hearth or birds that scream i’ the air? Did they not point at me as doomed to slay My father? but he’s dead and in his grave And here am I who ne’er unsheathed a sword; Unless the longing for his absent son Killed him and so _I_ slew him in a sense. But, as they stand, the oracles are dead— Dust, ashes, nothing, dead as Polybus.

items.chapter: Scene: Thebes. Before the Palace of Oedipus.
items.text: JOCASTA. Why should a mortal man, the sport of chance, With no assured foreknowledge, be afraid? Best live a careless life from hand to mouth. This wedlock with thy mother fear not thou. How oft it chances that in dreams a man Has wed his mother! He who least regards Such brainsick phantasies lives most at ease.

items.chapter: Scene: Thebes. Before the Palace of Oedipus.
items.text: MESSENGER. Who may this woman be whom thus you fear?

items.chapter: Scene: Thebes. Before the Palace of Oedipus.
items.text: MESSENGER. Was this the fear that exiled thee from home?

items.chapter: Scene: Thebes. Before the Palace of Oedipus.
items.text: OEDIPUS. Nay, I will ne’er go near my parents more.

items.chapter: Scene: Thebes. Before the Palace of Oedipus.
items.text: MESSENGER. Lest through thy parents thou shouldst be accursed?

items.chapter: Scene: Thebes. Before the Palace of Oedipus.
items.text: MESSENGER. Since Polybus was naught to thee in blood.

items.chapter: Scene: Thebes. Before the Palace of Oedipus.
items.text: OEDIPUS. What reason had he then to call me son?

items.chapter: Scene: Thebes. Before the Palace of Oedipus.
items.text: MESSENGER. I found thee in Cithaeron’s wooded glens.

items.chapter: Scene: Thebes. Before the Palace of Oedipus.
items.text: OEDIPUS. My savior? from what harm? what ailed me then?

items.chapter: Scene: Thebes. Before the Palace of Oedipus.
items.text: MESSENGER. Whence thou deriv’st the name that still is thine.

items.chapter: Scene: Thebes. Before the Palace of Oedipus.
items.text: MESSENGER. Not I; another shepherd gave thee me.

items.chapter: Scene: Thebes. Before the Palace of Oedipus.
items.text: OEDIPUS. And is he living still for me to see him?

items.chapter: Scene: Thebes. Before the Palace of Oedipus.
items.text: JOCASTA. Who is the man? What matter? Let it be. ’Twere waste of thought to weigh such idle words.

items.chapter: Scene: Thebes. Before the Palace of Oedipus.
items.text: OEDIPUS. I cannot; I must probe this matter home.

items.chapter: Scene: Thebes. Before the Palace of Oedipus.
items.text: OEDIPUS. Go, fetch me here the herd, and leave yon woman To glory in her pride of ancestry.

items.chapter: Scene: Thebes. Before the Palace of Oedipus.
items.text: (Ant.) Child, who bare thee, nymph or goddess? sure thy sure was more than man, Haply the hill-roamer Pan. Of did Loxias beget thee, for he haunts the upland wold; Or Cyllene’s lord, or Bacchus, dweller on the hilltops cold? Did some Heliconian Oread give him thee, a new-born joy? Nymphs with whom he love to toy?

items.chapter: Scene: Thebes. Before the Palace of Oedipus.
items.text: HERDSMAN. I was, a thrall, not purchased but home-bred.

items.chapter: Scene: Thebes. Before the Palace of Oedipus.
items.text: OEDIPUS. Then there Thou must have known yon man, at least by fame?

items.chapter: Scene: Thebes. Before the Palace of Oedipus.
items.text: HERDSMAN. ’Tis long ago, but all thou say’st is true.

items.chapter: Scene: Thebes. Before the Palace of Oedipus.
items.text: HERDSMAN. A plague upon thee! Hold thy wanton tongue!

items.chapter: Scene: Thebes. Before the Palace of Oedipus.
items.text: OEDIPUS. If thou lack’st grace to speak, I’ll loose thy tongue.

items.chapter: Scene: Thebes. Before the Palace of Oedipus.
items.text: HERDSMAN. I did; and would that I had died that day!

items.chapter: Scene: Thebes. Before the Palace of Oedipus.
items.text: OEDIPUS. Whence came it? was it thine, or given to thee?

items.chapter: Scene: Thebes. Before the Palace of Oedipus.
items.text: OEDIPUS. If I must question thee again, thou’rt lost.

items.chapter: Scene: Thebes. Before the Palace of Oedipus.
items.text: HERDSMAN. Know then the child was by repute his own, But she within, thy consort best could tell.

items.chapter: Scene: Thebes. Before the Palace of Oedipus.
items.text: CHORUS. (Str. 1) Races of mortal man Whose life is but a span, I count ye but the shadow of a shade! For he who most doth know Of bliss, hath but the show; A moment, and the visions pale and fade. Thy fall, O Oedipus, thy piteous fall Warns me none born of women blest to call.

items.chapter: Scene: Thebes. Before the Palace of Oedipus.
items.text: CHORUS. Grievous enough for all our tears and groans Our past calamities; what canst thou add?

items.chapter: Scene: Thebes. Before the Palace of Oedipus.
items.text: He tore the golden brooches that upheld Her queenly robes, upraised them high and smote Full on his eye-balls, uttering words like these: “No more shall ye behold such sights of woe, Deeds I have suffered and myself have wrought; Henceforward quenched in darkness shall ye see Those ye should ne’er have seen; now blind to those Whom, when I saw, I vainly yearned to know.” Such was the burden of his moan, whereto, Not once but oft, he struck with his hand uplift His eyes, and at each stroke the ensanguined orbs Bedewed his beard, not oozing drop by drop, But one black gory downpour, thick as hail. Such evils, issuing from the double source, Have whelmed them both, confounding man and wife. Till now the storied fortune of this house Was fortunate indeed; but from this day Woe, lamentation, ruin, death, disgrace, All ills that can be named, all, all are theirs.

items.chapter: Scene: Thebes. Before the Palace of Oedipus.
items.text: OEDIPUS. Ah me! ah woe is me! Ah whither am I borne! How like a ghost forlorn My voice flits from me on the air! On, on the demon goads. The end, ah where?

items.chapter: Scene: Thebes. Before the Palace of Oedipus.
items.text: CHORUS. O doer of dread deeds, how couldst thou mar Thy vision thus? What demon goaded thee?

items.chapter: Scene: Thebes. Before the Palace of Oedipus.
items.text: OEDIPUS. Then had I never come to shed My father’s blood nor climbed my mother’s bed; The monstrous offspring of a womb defiled, Co-mate of him who gendered me, and child. Was ever man before afflicted thus, Like Oedipus.

items.chapter: Scene: Thebes. Before the Palace of Oedipus.
items.text: CREON. Lo, here is Creon, the one man to grant Thy prayer by action or advice, for he Is left the State’s sole guardian in thy stead.

items.chapter: Scene: Thebes. Before the Palace of Oedipus.
items.text: CREON. And what the favor thou wouldst crave of me?

items.chapter: Scene: Thebes. Before the Palace of Oedipus.
items.text: OEDIPUS. Dare ye inquire concerning such a wretch?

items.chapter: Scene: Thebes. Before the Palace of Oedipus.
items.text: OEDIPUS. God speed thee! and as meed for bringing them May Providence deal with thee kindlier Than it has dealt with me! O children mine, Where are ye? Let me clasp you with these hands, A brother’s hands, a father’s; hands that made Lack-luster sockets of his once bright eyes; Hands of a man who blindly, recklessly, Became your sire by her from whom he sprang. Though I cannot behold you, I must weep In thinking of the evil days to come, The slights and wrongs that men will put upon you. Where’er ye go to feast or festival, No merrymaking will it prove for you, But oft abashed in tears ye will return. And when ye come to marriageable years, Where’s the bold wooers who will jeopardize To take unto himself such disrepute As to my children’s children still must cling, For what of infamy is lacking here?

items.chapter: Scene: Thebes. Before the Palace of Oedipus.
items.text: CHORUS. Look ye, countrymen and Thebans, this is Oedipus the great, He who knew the Sphinx’s riddle and was mightiest in our state. Who of all our townsmen gazed not on his fame with envious eyes? Now, in what a sea of troubles sunk and overwhelmed he lies! Therefore wait to see life’s ending ere thou count one mortal blest; Wait till free from pain and sorrow he has gained his final rest.

items.chapter: Scene: Thebes. Before the Palace of Oedipus.
items.text: Oedipus, the blind and banished King of Thebes, has come in his wanderings to Colonus, a deme of Athens, led by his daughter Antigone. He sits to rest on a rock just within a sacred grove of the Furies and is bidden depart by a passing native. But Oedipus, instructed by an oracle that he had reached his final resting-place, refuses to stir, and the stranger consents to go and consult the Elders of Colonus (the Chorus of the Play). Conducted to the spot they pity at first the blind beggar and his daughter, but on learning his name they are horror-striken and order him to quit the land. He appeals to the world-famed hospitality of Athens and hints at the blessings that his coming will confer on the State. They agree to await the decision of King Theseus. From Theseus Oedipus craves protection in life and burial in Attic soil; the benefits that will accrue shall be told later.

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 1
items.text: Enter the blind OEDIPUS led by his daughter, ANTIGONE.

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 1
items.text: OEDIPUS. Say, prithee, if thou knowest, where we are.

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 1
items.text: OEDIPUS. What, moving hitherward and on his way?

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 1
items.text: STRANGER. Inviolable, untrod; goddesses, Dread brood of Earth and Darkness, here abide.

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 1
items.text: STRANGER. Nay, ’tis not mine to bid thee hence without Due warrant and instruction from the State.

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 1
items.text: OEDIPUS. Thou sayest there are dwellers in these parts?

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 1
items.text: STRANGER. Theseus, the son of Aegeus our late king.

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 1
items.text: OEDIPUS. The blind man’s words will be instinct with sight.

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 1
items.text: Hear, gentle daughters of primeval Night, Hear, namesake of great Pallas; Athens, first Of cities, pity this dishonored shade, The ghost of him who once was Oedipus.

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 1
items.text: OEDIPUS. I am that man; I know you near Ears to the blind, they say, are eyes.

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 1
items.text: ANTIGONE. We must obey and do as here they do.

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 1
items.text: CHORUS. In a strange land strange thou art; To her will incline thy heart; Honor whatso’er the State Honors, all she frowns on hate.

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 1
items.text: ANTIGONE. Thy steps to my steps, lean thine aged frame on mine.

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 1
items.text: OEDIPUS. Forbear, nor urge me further to reveal—

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 1
items.text: OEDIPUS. I will; no plea for silence can I urge.

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 1
items.text: ANTIGONE. O sirs! ye suffered not my father blind, Albeit gracious and to ruth inclined, Knowing the deeds he wrought, not innocent, But with no ill intent; Yet heed a maiden’s moan Who pleads for him alone; My eyes, not reft of sight, Plead with you as a daughter’s might You are our providence, O make us not go hence! O with a gracious nod Grant us the nigh despaired-of boon we crave? Hear us, O hear, But all that ye hold dear, Wife, children, homestead, hearth and God! Where will you find one, search ye ne’er so well. Who ’scapes perdition if a god impel!

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 1
items.text: OEDIPUS. Where is he, strangers, he who sways the realm?

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 1
items.text: OEDIPUS. Well, may he come with blessing to his State And me! Who serves his neighbor serves himself. 5

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 1
items.text: ISMENE. Father and sister, names to me most sweet, How hardly have I found you, hardly now When found at last can see you through my tears!

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 1
items.text: And now what mission summons thee from home, What news, Ismene, hast thou for thy father? This much I know, thou com’st not empty-handed, Without a warning of some new alarm.

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 1
items.text: ISMENE. Thy country (so it runs) shall yearn in time To have thee for their weal alive or dead.

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 1
items.text: OEDIPUS. Poor help to raise an old man fallen in youth.

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 1
items.text: OEDIPUS. Thy tomb, If disappointed, brings on them a curse.

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 1
items.text: OEDIPUS. Then never shall they be my masters, never!

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 1
items.text: ISMENE. Envoys who visited the Delphic hearth.

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 1
items.text: OEDIPUS. They knew it, yet the ignoble greed of rule Outweighed all longing for their sire’s return.

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 1
items.text: CHORUS. Our pity, Oedipus, thou needs must move, Thou and these maidens; and the stronger plea Thou urgest, as the savior of our land, Disposes me to counsel for thy weal.

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 1
items.text: CHORUS. Make a libation first of water fetched With undefiled hands from living spring.

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 1
items.text: OEDIPUS. What next? how must I end the ritual?

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 1
items.text: CHORUS. With water and with honey; add no wine.

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 1
items.text: OEDIPUS. Hear ye, my daughters, what these strangers say?

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 1
items.text: CHORUS. Beyond this grove; if thou hast need of aught, The guardian of the close will lend his aid.

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 1
items.text: CHORUS. The tale is bruited far and near, And echoes still from ear to ear. The truth, I fain would hear.

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 1
items.text: OEDIPUS. It stabs me like a sword, That two-edged word, O stranger, but these maids—my own—

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 1
items.text: OEDIPUS. I served the State; would I had never won That graceless grace by which I was undone.

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 1
items.text: THESEUS. Oft had I heard of thee in times gone by— The bloody mutilation of thine eyes— And therefore know thee, son of Laius. All that I lately gathered on the way Made my conjecture doubly sure; and now Thy garb and that marred visage prove to me That thou art he. So pitying thine estate, Most ill-starred Oedipus, I fain would know What is the suit ye urge on me and Athens, Thou and the helpless maiden at thy side. Declare it; dire indeed must be the tale Whereat _I_ should recoil. I too was reared, Like thee, in exile, and in foreign lands Wrestled with many perils, no man more. Wherefore no alien in adversity Shall seek in vain my succor, nor shalt thou; I know myself a mortal, and my share In what the morrow brings no more than thine.

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 1
items.text: THESEUS. What profit dost thou proffer to have brought?

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 1
items.text: OEDIPUS. Yea, the last boon is warrant for the rest.

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 1
items.text: THESEUS. If there be no compulsion, then methinks To rest in banishment befits not thee.

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 1
items.text: OEDIPUS. O Theseus, I have suffered wrongs on wrongs.

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 1
items.text: OEDIPUS. My case stands thus; by my own flesh and blood I was expelled my country, and can ne’er Thither return again, a parricide.

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 1
items.text: OEDIPUS. Dear son of Aegeus, to the gods alone Is given immunity from eld and death; But nothing else escapes all-ruinous time. Earth’s might decays, the might of men decays, Honor grows cold, dishonor flourishes, There is no constancy ’twixt friend and friend, Or city and city; be it soon or late, Sweet turns to bitter, hate once more to love. If now ’tis sunshine betwixt Thebes and thee And not a cloud, Time in his endless course Gives birth to endless days and nights, wherein The merest nothing shall suffice to cut With serried spears your bonds of amity. Then shall my slumbering and buried corpse In its cold grave drink their warm life-blood up, If Zeus be Zeus and Phoebus still speak true.

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 1
items.text: THESEUS. What dost thou then decide—to come with me?

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 1
items.text: OEDIPUS. Such shall it prove, if thou fulfill’st thy pledge.

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 1
items.text: CHORUS. (Str. 1) Thou hast come to a steed-famed land for rest, O stranger worn with toil, To a land of all lands the goodliest Colonus’ glistening soil. ’Tis the haunt of the clear-voiced nightingale, Who hid in her bower, among The wine-dark ivy that wreathes the vale, Trilleth her ceaseless song; And she loves, where the clustering berries nod O’er a sunless, windless glade, The spot by no mortal footstep trod, The pleasance kept for the Bacchic god, Where he holds each night his revels wild With the nymphs who fostered the lusty child.

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 1
items.text: ANTIGONE. Oh land extolled above all lands, ’tis now For thee to make these glorious titles good.

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 1
items.text: OEDIPUS. O front of brass, thy subtle tongue would twist To thy advantage every plea of right Why try thy arts on me, why spread again Toils where ’twould gall me sorest to be snared? In old days when by self-wrought woes distraught, I yearned for exile as a glad release, Thy will refused the favor then I craved. But when my frenzied grief had spent its force, And I was fain to taste the sweets of home, Then thou wouldst thrust me from my country, then These ties of kindred were by thee ignored; And now again when thou behold’st this State And all its kindly people welcome me, Thou seek’st to part us, wrapping in soft words Hard thoughts. And yet what pleasure canst thou find In forcing friendship on unwilling foes?

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 1
items.text: CREON. Unhappy man, will years ne’er make thee wise? Must thou live on to cast a slur on age?

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 1
items.text: OEDIPUS. Depart! I bid thee in these burghers’ name, And prowl no longer round me to blockade My destined harbor.

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 1
items.text: CREON. One of thy daughters is already seized, The other I will carry off anon.

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 1
items.text: CREON. I meddle not with him, but her who is mine.

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 1
items.text: ANTIGONE. Ah, woe is me, they drag me hence, O friends.

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 1
items.text: CHORUS. Unless perchance our sovereign intervene.

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 1
items.text: CREON. Nothing shall curb my will; though I be old And single-handed, I will have this man.

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 1
items.text: CHORUS. Aye words, but not yet deeds, Zeus knoweth!

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 1
items.text: OEDIPUS. Creon who stands before thee. He it is Hath robbed me of my all, my daughters twain.

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 1
items.text: CREON. Not deeming this city void of men Or counsel, son of Aegeus, as thou say’st I did what I have done; rather I thought Your people were not like to set such store by kin of mine and keep them ’gainst my will. Nor would they harbor, so I stood assured, A godless parricide, a reprobate Convicted of incestuous marriage ties. For on her native hill of Ares here (I knew your far-famed Areopagus) Sits Justice, and permits not vagrant folk To stay within your borders. In that faith I hunted down my quarry; and e’en then I had refrained but for the curses dire Wherewith he banned my kinsfolk and myself: Such wrong, methought, had warrant for my act. Anger has no old age but only death; The dead alone can feel no touch of spite. So thou must work thy will; my cause is just But weak without allies; yet will I try, Old as I am, to answer deeds with deeds.

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 1
items.text: THESEUS. Enough of words; the captors speed amain, While we the victims stand debating here.

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 2
items.text: THESEUS. Threaten us and—begone! Thou, Oedipus, Stay here assured that nothing save my death Will stay my purpose to restore the maids.

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 2
items.text: (Str. 2) Fight they or now prepare To fight? a vision rare Tells me that soon again I shall behold the twain Maidens so ill bestead, By their kin buffeted. Today, today Zeus worketh some great thing This day shall victory bring. O for the wings, the wings of a dove, To be borne with the speed of the gale, Up and still upwards to sail And gaze on the fray from the clouds above. (Ant. 2) All-seeing Zeus, O lord of heaven, To our guardian host be given Might triumphant to surprise Flying foes and win their prize. Hear us, Zeus, and hear us, child Of Zeus, Athene undefiled, Hear, Apollo, hunter, hear, Huntress, sister of Apollo, Who the dappled swift-foot deer O’er the wooded glade dost follow; Help with your two-fold power Athens in danger’s hour! O wayfarer, thou wilt not have to tax The friends who watch for thee with false presage, For lo, an escort with the maids draws near.

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 2
items.text: OEDIPUS. I have my darlings, and if death should come, Death were not wholly bitter with you near. Cling to me, press me close on either side, There rest ye from your dreary wayfaring. Now tell me of your ventures, but in brief; Brief speech suffices for young maids like you.

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 2
items.text: THESEUS. ’Tis said a man, no countryman of thine, But of thy kin, hath taken sanctuary Beside the altar of Poseidon, where I was at sacrifice when called away.

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 2
items.text: THESEUS. Think if there be not any of thy kin At Argos who might claim this boon of thee.

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 2
items.text: THESEUS. Thou sure mightest listen. If his suit offend, No need to grant it. Why so loth to hear him?

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 2
items.text: OEDIPUS. Grievous to me, my child, the boon ye win By pleading. Let it be then; have your way Only if come he must, I beg thee, friend, Let none have power to dispose of me.

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 2
items.text: ANTIGONE. The same that we surmised. From the outset—Polyneices. He is here. [Enter POLYNEICES]

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 2
items.text: So likewise hold the soothsayers, for when I came to Argos in the Dorian land And took the king Adrastus’ child to wife, Under my standard I enlisted all The foremost captains of the Apian isle, To levy with their aid that sevenfold host Of spearmen against Thebes, determining To oust my foes or die in a just cause. Why then, thou askest, am I here today? Father, I come a suppliant to thee Both for myself and my allies who now With squadrons seven beneath their seven spears Beleaguer all the plain that circles Thebes.

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 2
items.text: OEDIPUS. Nay, worthy seniors, but for Theseus’ sake Who sent him hither to have word of me. Never again would he have heard my voice; But now he shall obtain this parting grace, An answer that will bring him little joy. O villain, when thou hadst the sovereignty That now thy brother holdeth in thy stead, Didst thou not drive me, thine own father, out, An exile, cityless, and make we wear This beggar’s garb thou weepest to behold, Now thou art come thyself to my sad plight? Nothing is here for tears; it must be borne By _me_ till death, and I shall think of thee As of my murderer; thou didst thrust me out; ’Tis thou hast made me conversant with woe, Through thee I beg my bread in a strange land; And had not these my daughters tended me I had been dead for aught of aid from thee.

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 2
items.text: ANTIGONE. One boon, O Polyneices, let me crave.

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 2
items.text: POLYNEICES. ’Tis shame to live in exile, and shall I The elder bear a younger brother’s flouts?

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 2
items.text: ANTIGONE. Misguided youth, thy purpose then stands fast!

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 2
items.text: CHORUS. (Str. 1) Ills on ills! no pause or rest! Come they from our sightless guest? Or haply now we see fulfilled What fate long time hath willed? For ne’er have I proved vain Aught that the heavenly powers ordain. Time with never sleeping eye Watches what is writ on high, Overthrowing now the great, Raising now from low estate. Hark! How the thunder rumbles! Zeus defend us!

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 2
items.text: CHORUS. (Ant. 1) Hark! with louder, nearer roar The bolt of Zeus descends once more. My spirit quails and cowers: my hair Bristles for fear. Again that flare! What doth the lightning-flash portend? Ever it points to issues grave. Dread powers of air! Save, Zeus, O save!

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 2
items.text: OEDIPUS. Is the prince coming? Will he when he comes Find me yet living and my senses clear!

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 2
items.text: OEDIPUS. Thou com’st much wished for, Prince, and sure some god Hath bid good luck attend thee on thy way.

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 2
items.text: THESEUS. How sayest thou they signify their will?

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 2
items.text: But to the spot—the god within me goads— Let us set forth no longer hesitate. Follow me, daughters, this way. Strange that I Whom you have led so long should lead you now. Oh, touch me not, but let me all alone Find out the sepulcher that destiny Appoints me in this land. Hither, this way, For this way Hermes leads, the spirit guide, And Persephassa, empress of the dead. O light, no light to me, but mine erewhile, Now the last time I feel thee palpable, For I am drawing near the final gloom Of Hades. Blessing on thee, dearest friend, On thee and on thy land and followers! Live prosperous and in your happy state Still for your welfare think on me, the dead. [Exit THESEUS followed by ANTIGONE and ISMENE]

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 2
items.text: CHORUS. How? By a god-sent, painless doom, poor soul?

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 2
items.text: It was a messenger from heaven, or else Some gentle, painless cleaving of earth’s base; For without wailing or disease or pain He passed away—and end most marvelous. And if to some my tale seems foolishness I am content that such could count me fool.

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 2
items.text: ISMENE. I know not. O that Death Might nip my breath, And let me share my aged father’s fate. I cannot live a life thus desolate.

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 2
items.text: CHORUS. His end was blessed; therefore, children, stay Your sorrow. Man is born to fate a prey.

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 2
items.text: CHORUS. Sure ye are driven on the breakers’ surge.

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 2
items.text: ANTIGONE. Well, if he would have it so, We must yield. Then let us go Back to Thebes, if yet we may Heal this mortal feud and stay The self-wrought doom That drives our brothers to their tomb.

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 2
items.text: 6 (return) [ Creon desires to bury Oedipus on the confines of Thebes so as to avoid the pollution and yet offer due rites at his tomb. Ismene tells him of the latest oracle and interprets to him its purport, that some day the Theban invaders of Athens will be routed in a battle near the grave of Oedipus.]

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 2
items.text: ANTIGONE and ISMENE—daughters of Oedipus and sisters of Polyneices and Eteocles. CREON, King of Thebes. HAEMON, Son of Creon, betrothed to Antigone. EURYDICE, wife of Creon. TEIRESIAS, the prophet. CHORUS, of Theban elders. A WATCHMAN A MESSENGER A SECOND MESSENGER

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 2
items.text: ISMENE. What is it? Some dark secret stirs thy breast.

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 2
items.text: ANTIGONE. Lend me a hand to bear the corpse away.

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 2
items.text: ISMENE. Bethink thee, sister, of our father’s fate, Abhorred, dishonored, self-convinced of sin, Blinded, himself his executioner. Think of his mother-wife (ill sorted names) Done by a noose herself had twined to death And last, our hapless brethren in one day, Both in a mutual destiny involved, Self-slaughtered, both the slayer and the slain. Bethink thee, sister, we are left alone; Shall we not perish wretchedest of all, If in defiance of the law we cross A monarch’s will?—weak women, think of that, Not framed by nature to contend with men. Remember this too that the stronger rules; We must obey his orders, these or worse. Therefore I plead compulsion and entreat The dead to pardon. I perforce obey The powers that be. ’Tis foolishness, I ween, To overstep in aught the golden mean.

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 2
items.text: ANTIGONE. O waste no fears on me; look to thyself.

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 2
items.text: ISMENE. If thou succeed; but thou art doomed to fail.

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 2
items.text: ISMENE. Have thine own way then; ’tis a mad endeavor, Yet to thy lovers thou art dear as ever. [Exeunt]

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 2
items.text: (Ant. 2) Now Victory to Thebes returns again And smiles upon her chariot-circled plain. Now let feast and festal should Memories of war blot out. Let us to the temples throng, Dance and sing the live night long. God of Thebes, lead thou the round. Bacchus, shaker of the ground! Let us end our revels here; Lo! Creon our new lord draws near, Crowned by this strange chance, our king. What, I marvel, pondering? Why this summons? Wherefore call Us, his elders, one and all, Bidding us with him debate, On some grave concern of State? [Enter CREON]

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 2
items.text: CHORUS. On younger shoulders lay this grievous charge.

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 2
items.text: GUARD. My lord, I will not make pretense to pant And puff as some light-footed messenger. In sooth my soul beneath its pack of thought Made many a halt and turned and turned again; For conscience plied her spur and curb by turns. “Why hurry headlong to thy fate, poor fool?” She whispered. Then again, “If Creon learn This from another, thou wilt rue it worse.” Thus leisurely I hastened on my road; Much thought extends a furlong to a league. But in the end the forward voice prevailed, To face thee. I will speak though I say nothing. For plucking courage from despair methought, ‘Let the worst hap, thou canst but meet thy fate.’

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 2
items.text: GUARD. The bearer of dread tidings needs must quake.

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 2
items.text: Our quest was at a standstill, when one spake And bowed us all to earth like quivering reeds, For there was no gainsaying him nor way To escape perdition: _Ye_are_bound_to_tell_ _The_King,_ye_cannot_hide_it; so he spake. And he convinced us all; so lots were cast, And I, unlucky scapegoat, drew the prize. So here I am unwilling and withal Unwelcome; no man cares to hear ill news.

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 2
items.text: CREON. Begone! canst thou not see That e’en this question irks me?

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 2
items.text: GUARD. Babbler perchance, but innocent of the crime.

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 3
items.text: CHORUS. (Str. 1) Many wonders there be, but naught more wondrous than man; Over the surging sea, with a whitening south wind wan, Through the foam of the firth, man makes his perilous way; And the eldest of deities Earth that knows not toil nor decay Ever he furrows and scores, as his team, year in year out, With breed of the yoked horse, the ploughshare turneth about.

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 3
items.text: What strange vision meets my eyes, Fills me with a wild surprise? Sure I know her, sure ’tis she, The maid Antigone. Hapless child of hapless sire, Didst thou recklessly conspire, Madly brave the King’s decree? Therefore are they haling thee? [Enter GUARD bringing ANTIGONE]

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 3
items.text: CREON. Say, how didst thou arrest the maid, and where?

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 3
items.text: GUARD. It happened thus. No sooner had we come, Driven from thy presence by those awful threats, Than straight we swept away all trace of dust, And bared the clammy body. Then we sat High on the ridge to windward of the stench, While each man kept he fellow alert and rated Roundly the sluggard if he chanced to nap. So all night long we watched, until the sun Stood high in heaven, and his blazing beams Smote us. A sudden whirlwind then upraised A cloud of dust that blotted out the sky, And swept the plain, and stripped the woodlands bare, And shook the firmament. We closed our eyes And waited till the heaven-sent plague should pass. At last it ceased, and lo! there stood this maid.

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 3
items.text: CREON. And yet wert bold enough to break the law?

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 3
items.text: More hateful still the miscreant who seeks When caught, to make a virtue of a crime.

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 3
items.text: ANTIGONE. These think as I, but bate their breath to thee.

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 3
items.text: CREON. Why cast a slur on one by honoring one?

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 3
items.text: CREON. Not that the base should fare as do the brave.

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 3
items.text: CHORUS. Lo from out the palace gate, Weeping o’er her sister’s fate, Comes Ismene; see her brow, Once serene, beclouded now, See her beauteous face o’erspread With a flush of angry red.

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 3
items.text: ISMENE. But now thy bark is stranded, I am bold To claim my share as partner in the loss.

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 3
items.text: ANTIGONE. Ask Creon, he’s thy kinsman and best friend.

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 3
items.text: ANTIGONE. Yea, for thou chosed’st life, and I to die.

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 3
items.text: CREON. Both maids, methinks, are crazed. One suddenly Has lost her wits, the other was born mad.

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 3
items.text: CREON. Say not thy sister _here_: thy sister’s dead.

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 3
items.text: CREON. A plague on thee and thy accursed bride!

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 3
items.text: CHORUS. (Str. 1) Thrice blest are they who never tasted pain! If once the curse of Heaven attaint a race, The infection lingers on and speeds apace, Age after age, and each the cup must drain.

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 3
items.text: Past, present, and to be, All bow to thy decree, All that exceeds the mean by Fate Is punished, Love or Hate.

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 3
items.text: CREON. Well spoken: so right-minded sons should feel, In all deferring to a father’s will. For ’tis the hope of parents they may rear A brood of sons submissive, keen to avenge Their father’s wrongs, and count his friends their own. But who begets unprofitable sons, He verily breeds trouble for himself, And for his foes much laughter. Son, be warned And let no woman fool away thy wits. Ill fares the husband mated with a shrew, And her embraces very soon wax cold. For what can wound so surely to the quick As a false friend? So spue and cast her off, Bid her go find a husband with the dead. For since I caught her openly rebelling, Of all my subjects the one malcontent, I will not prove a traitor to the State. She surely dies. Go, let her, if she will, Appeal to Zeus the God of Kindred, for If thus I nurse rebellion in my house, Shall not I foster mutiny without?

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 3
items.text: O father, nothing is by me more prized Than thy well-being, for what higher good Can children covet than their sire’s fair fame, As fathers too take pride in glorious sons? Therefore, my father, cling not to one mood, And deemed not thou art right, all others wrong. For whoso thinks that wisdom dwells with him, That he alone can speak or think aright, Such oracles are empty breath when tried. The wisest man will let himself be swayed By others’ wisdom and relax in time. See how the trees beside a stream in flood Save, if they yield to force, each spray unharmed, But by resisting perish root and branch. The mariner who keeps his mainsheet taut, And will not slacken in the gale, is like To sail with thwarts reversed, keel uppermost.

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 3
items.text: CREON. Strange merit this to sanction lawlessness!

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 3
items.text: HAEMON. A State for one man is no State at all.

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 3
items.text: CREON. O reprobate, would’st wrangle with thy sire?

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 3
items.text: CREON. O heart corrupt, a woman’s minion thou!

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 3
items.text: HAEMON. So she shall die, but one will die with her.

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 3
items.text: CREON. Play not the spaniel, thou a woman’s slave.

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 3
items.text: CREON. Let him go vent his fury like a fiend: These sisters twain he shall not save from death.

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 3
items.text: (Ant). Mad are thy subjects all, and even the wisest heart Straight to folly will fall, at a touch of thy poisoned dart. Thou didst kindle the strife, this feud of kinsman with kin, By the eyes of a winsome wife, and the yearning her heart to win. For as her consort still, enthroned with Justice above, Thou bendest man to thy will, O all invincible Love.

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 3
items.text: ANTIGONE. (Ant. 1) Nay, but the piteous tale I’ve heard men tell Of Tantalus’ doomed child, Chained upon Siphylus’ high rocky fell, That clung like ivy wild, Drenched by the pelting rain and whirling snow, Left there to pine, While on her frozen breast the tears aye flow— Her fate is mine.

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 3
items.text: CHORUS. Religion has her chains, ’tis true, Let rite be paid when rites are due. Yet is it ill to disobey The powers who hold by might the sway. Thou hast withstood authority, A self-willed rebel, thou must die.

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 3
items.text: CHORUS. The same ungovernable will Drives like a gale the maiden still.

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 3
items.text: CHORUS. (Str. 1) Like to thee that maiden bright, Danae, in her brass-bound tower, Once exchanged the glad sunlight For a cell, her bridal bower. And yet she sprang of royal line, My child, like thine, And nursed the seed By her conceived Of Zeus descending in a golden shower. Strange are the ways of Fate, her power Nor wealth, nor arms withstand, nor tower; Nor brass-prowed ships, that breast the sea From Fate can flee.

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 3
items.text: TEIRESIAS. Princes of Thebes, two wayfarers as one, Having betwixt us eyes for one, we are here. The blind man cannot move without a guide.

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 3
items.text: CREON. What is this? Thy words inspire a dread presentiment.

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 3
items.text: CREON. Is this the prelude to some hackneyed saw?

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 3
items.text: TEIRESIAS. And yet thou say’st my prophesies are frauds.

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 3
items.text: CREON. Skilled prophet art thou, but to wrong inclined.

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 3
items.text: CREON. Be sure thou wilt not traffic on my wits.

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 3
items.text: CHORUS. Son of Menoeceus, list to good advice.

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 3
items.text: CREON. Ah! what a wrench it is to sacrifice My heart’s resolve; but Fate is ill to fight.

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 3
items.text: Where Ismenus rolls his waters, Where the Dragon’s teeth were sown, Where the Bacchanals thy daughters Round thee roam, There thy home; Thebes, O Bacchus, is thine own.

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 3
items.text: (Ant. 2) Brightest of all the orbs that breathe forth light, Authentic son of Zeus, immortal king, Leader of all the voices of the night, Come, and thy train of Thyiads with thee bring, Thy maddened rout Who dance before thee all night long, and shout, Thy handmaids we, Evoe, Evoe!

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 3
items.text: MESSENGER. Haemon; his blood shed by no stranger hand.

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 3
items.text: CHORUS. Lo! from the palace gates I see approaching Creon’s unhappy wife, Eurydice. Comes she by chance or learning her son’s fate? [Enter EURYDICE]

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 3
items.text: CHORUS. What makest thou of this? The Queen has gone Without a word importing good or ill.

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 3
items.text: CREON. (Str. 1) Woe for sin of minds perverse, Deadly fraught with mortal curse. Behold us slain and slayers, all akin. Woe for my counsel dire, conceived in sin. Alas, my son, Life scarce begun, Thou wast undone. The fault was mine, mine only, O my son!

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 3
items.text: CREON. What woe is lacking to my tale of woes?

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 3
items.text: SECOND MESSENGER. Beside the altar on a keen-edged sword She fell and closed her eyes in night, but erst She mourned for Megareus who nobly died Long since, then for her son; with her last breath She cursed thee, the slayer of her child.

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 3
items.text: CREON. (Str. 4) I am the guilty cause. I did the deed, Thy murderer. Yea, I guilty plead. My henchmen, lead me hence, away, away, A cipher, less than nothing; no delay!

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 3
items.text: CHORUS. O pray not, prayers are idle; from the doom Of fate for mortals refuge is there none.

items.chapter: Scene: In front of the grove of the Eumenides. · 3
